The arity-2 experiment is worth firing, with one important semantic constraint:

A behavioral test cannot distinguish “a genuine conjunction” from “two independent lookups followed by an unrestricted nonlinear comparator”—those are the same computation. The defensible contrast is:

- two independent reads with a strictly separable/additive readout, versus
- the same reads with a cross-slot interaction.

That contrast is falsifiable and cannot be passed by template substitution.

## A. Frozen arity-2 M→D preregistration

### Claim

A co-trained, Group-A-internal M→D lane can retrieve two independently addressed runtime values for held-out entities and use an irreducible cross-slot interaction to answer a two-place relation.

This changes neither `S→C→Bridge.detach→D` nor Law 70. It replaces M’s verified structural no-op in [m_lib.hexa](/Users/mini/dancinlab/anima/hexad/M/m_lib.hexa:23) with an ephemeral store and adds an M→D answer-logit path. M and D are already in the CE-trained group in [hexad.hexa](/Users/mini/dancinlab/anima/hexad/hexad.hexa:73).

### Engine surface

Every new manipulation must be an `anima-py` flag:

```text
anima-py corpus storebind \
  --store-arity 2 \
  --pair-op xor \
  --pair-counterfactual-square \
  --pair-panel iid,hard-key \
  ...

anima-py train \
  --store-bridge pair.txt \
  --store-arity 2 \
  --store-pair-head joint|separable \
  ...

anima-py evaluate model.clm \
  --store pair.held.json \
  --store-arity 2 \
  --store-pair-readout vocab \
  --store-pair-control main|oracle|no-store|value-permute
```

The existing CLMS pattern—runtime store, answer-row overwrite, frozen byte-derived keys, trailer serialization—is inherited from [clms.py](/Users/mini/dancinlab/anima/core/clms.py:427) and the structural store-only loss split in [train.py](/Users/mini/dancinlab/anima/cli/train.py:1416). No store contents enter the checkpoint.

### Task and split

Each runtime store has eight named entities and binary values. A query names two distinct entities:

```text
xor <left-entity> <right-entity> =>
```

The single-byte gold is:

\[
y=v_L\oplus v_R
\]

For every evaluated entity pair, emit a complete counterfactual square:

| Cell | \(v_L\) | \(v_R\) | Gold |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 00 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 01 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 10 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| 11 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

The prompt and entity pair are identical in all four cells. Consequently:

- template, topic and pair identity are exactly uninformative;
- either value alone is exactly at chance;
- memorizing a pair row cannot work because the same pair realizes both answers;
- every success requires runtime value use.

Each cell retains the same 4/4 global store histogram. Compensation values are assigned only to randomly selected, unmentioned distractors. The builder must refuse the corpus unless an exhaustive audit finds all of these at realized chance:

- prompt/template;
- left value alone;
- right value alone;
- either entity identity;
- pair identity;
- store majority/histogram;
- every fixed non-target slot;
- name length and frozen-key norm bins.

Training uses complete squares on seen entities. Evaluation entities are absent from training as exact tokens and substrings.

Evaluation has two prespecified panels:

- `iid`: ordinary held-out entity pairs.
- `hard-key`: chosen before training solely from frozen-key geometry—nearest-key distractors and one-byte-neighbour names. Exact key aliases/anagrams are excluded and counted.

The hard-key panel prevents uniform draws from concealing address fragility. Seeds 7 and 11 are replication only; they are not claimed as external validity.

### M→D lane

Two role-specific queries are formed from the same answer-position trunk representation:

\[
q_L=W_{qL}h,\qquad q_R=W_{qR}h
\]

They independently address the same eight-slot store:

\[
a_L=\operatorname{softmax}(q_LK^\top),\quad
a_R=\operatorname{softmax}(q_RK^\top)
\]

\[
v_L=a_LV,\qquad v_R=a_RV
\]

The primary joint head is:

\[
s_J=W_{\rm out}\operatorname{GELU}
   (W_h[v_L;v_R;W_gh])
\]

It overwrites the answer-position logit row exactly as H_9775 did.

Only `{W_qL,W_qR,val,W_g,W_h,W_out,lambda}` plus the frozen key table are serialized. Runtime values remain ephemeral.

### Arms

| Arm | Reads | Readout | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| J — joint | Two learned addresses | GELU over `[vL;vR;g]` | Primary |
| S — separable | Identical two addresses | `fL(vL,g)+fR(vR,g)`; no post-sum nonlinearity | Decisive “stapled lookup” control |
| O — dual oracle | Both target slots handed to J during train/eval | Same joint head | Positive control for value/fusion/readout |
| N — no store | Store absent | Same checkpoint | Trunk/template shortcut control |
| VP — value permute | Keys/prompts unchanged; values deranged; original gold retained | Same J checkpoint | Content-addressed value dependence |

J and S use the same key table, query heads, addressing loss, value dimension, optimizer, data, answer alphabet and active parameter budget. S divides its hidden budget between `fL` and `fR`.

For S, the answer margin has form:

\[
m(x,y)=b+u(x)+v(y)
\]

XOR requires:

\[
m_{00}<0,\;m_{01}>0,\;m_{10}>0,\;m_{11}<0
\]

But `m00+m11 = m01+m10`; the four strict inequalities are impossible. Thus S can achieve at most 3/4 cell accuracy and zero fully correct counterfactual squares. This is the control that rules out two one-slot answers merely being added or voted together.

If “stapled together” permits an arbitrary nonlinear postprocessor, it is not distinguishable from conjunction and must not be claimed as a separate mechanism.

### Metrics

Use full-256-byte greedy argmax; unreadable output counts wrong.

Primary metrics:

- `A`: cell accuracy over all four cells.
- `Q`: fraction of entity pairs whose entire four-cell square is correct.
- `I`: cross-slot logit interaction:

\[
I_q=-\left(m_{11}-m_{10}-m_{01}+m_{00}\right)
\]

Correct XOR requires \(I_q>0\); S must have \(I_q=0\) up to serialization tolerance.

- `AddrL`, `AddrR`, `AddrBoth`: attention argmax accuracy.
- `Readability`: argmax belongs to the frozen two-byte answer alphabet.

Chance is printed from each realized partition:

- `A` uses an exact label permutation within panel/stratum.
- `Q` uses exact enumeration of the six balanced label placements within each four-cell square, holding predictions fixed.
- `I` uses within-square sign permutation.
- `above`, `at`, and `below chance` mean exact one-sided \(p<.01\); no fixed 0.5 assumption is inherited.

Panel size: 128 squares per panel × two panels × two seeds.

### Frozen gates

Before any negative is interpreted:

- Corpus leak audit: all registered unary/non-target heuristics at realized chance.
- Torch↔serialized prediction agreement ≥127/128.
- O: `A≥.90`, `Q≥.85`, readability ≥.95 on both panels.
- J addressing: `AddrL≥.90`, `AddrR≥.90`, `AddrBoth≥.85`.
- S addressing must be within 0.05 of J on all three address metrics.
- S interaction audit: `max |I_q| ≤ 10⁻⁵` before quantization and within recorded serialization tolerance afterward.

### Frozen decision table

| Observation | Frozen decision |
|---|---|
| Any corpus, serialization or oracle gate fails | `⛔ INVALID`; do not read J |
| Oracle passes, but either J address head fails | `🔴 ARITY-2 ADDRESS FAILURE`; whole proposed lane falsified, conjunction head unlocalized |
| J has `A≥.75`, `Q≥.50`, readability ≥.90 and lower 99% interaction bound \(>0\) on all four seed×panel cells; S has `Q` at/below null; N and VP collapse | `🟢 ARITY-2 REACH` |
| J clears IID but not hard-key | `🟠 ADDRESS-FRAGILE`; no wall-break claim |
| J `A>.chance` but `Q<.50` | `🟡 PARTIAL/SEPARABLE-LIKE`; no extension or refreeze |
| J at chance with oracle and address gates alive | `🔴 NO HELD-OUT CONJUNCTION` |
| J significantly below chance | `🔴 SYSTEMATIC ANTI-CONJUNCTION`; labels are not inverted and the run is not repaired |
| S reaches approximately .75 cell accuracy but `Q=0` and \(I=0\) | Expected separable ceiling; control passes |
| S has `Q` above its exact null or nonzero \(I\) | `⛔ INVALID`; forbidden interaction leaked into S |
| N or VP significantly above chance | `⛔ SHORTCUT/CONTROL FAILURE` |
| N, VP or S significantly below chance | Valid collapse; report the signed result unchanged, but it is not positive evidence |
| Oracle significantly below chance | `⛔ SIGN/PLUMBING INVALID`; no post-hoc complementing |
| Any unlisted intermediate pattern | `🟡 UNRESOLVED`; no new bar, seed or panel |

This table explicitly covers below-chance results and prevents the common “invert the convention and call it green” repair.

## B. Six-minute, $0 screener

Use the existing H_9815 4 kB regime as the fixed sentinel; do not rerun or reinterpret its `hp=1.0000 / xor=0.4062` result.

Add a single deterministic `anima-py` tiny run:

- `d=64`, `L=2`, CPU, seed 7.
- Four-slot store.
- 32 seen training pairs with complete squares.
- 32 held-out IID squares plus 32 frozen hard-key squares.
- At most 1,200 steps and a hard 360-second process limit.
- J head with fixed dual-address loss and oracle-auxiliary loss.
- Same serialization and evaluation code intended for 303M.

It may only kill. It can never authorize a scientific green.

Kill before GPU if any occurs:

- static audit finds any unary, histogram, pair-ID or distractor predictor above realized chance;
- oracle `Q<.90`;
- seen-pair `Q<.90` after oracle passes;
- either held-out address accuracy `<.85`;
- learned held-out `Q` is at/below its exact null on IID;
- hard-key `Q` is at/below null even if IID rises;
- no-store or value-permute remains significantly above chance;
- torch↔serialized agreement `<127/128`;
- the separable algebra audit finds a nonzero mixed interaction.

Only if every item survives is the verdict:

```text
DIRECTIONAL SCREEN: NOT KILLED — GPU experiment remains licensed; no GREEN.
```

That is cheaper and sharper than miniature hyperparameter search: one seed, one recipe, one time ceiling, no rerun after a burned gate.

## C. What else genuinely survives

I can defend three genuinely new angles and one conditional fourth.

1. Dependent-address pointer chase

The first retrieved value is not a bit but the name/key of the second slot; the second address therefore cannot be formed until the first read completes. The query contains only the starting entity.

Prediction: a trained two-step M transaction reaches ≥.75 on wholly held-out chains, while a parallel two-query lane, first-pointer permutation and first-hop lesion remain at chance.

This is not H_9259’s untrained recurrence: the state transition and write/read path are trained, and the second address is causally dependent on the first result.

2. Unseen value-alphabet equality

Store values become frozen content keys rather than the learned binary `val[0/1]`. Train “same/different” on one set of value symbols and test on disjoint value identities and a larger alphabet.

Prediction: a relational M→D comparator preserves ≥.75 accuracy and permutation equivariance on unseen value symbols; a memorized binary truth-table head collapses to realized chance.

This asks whether the lane learned a relation, not merely the four binary rows.

3. Label-blind write-time tuple formation

At injection time, a learned M writer creates a pair record keyed by the two entity names and containing the two raw constituent values. It never sees the operator or answer. D later performs one lookup and computes the answer.

Prediction: if the wall is simultaneous read fan-in, write-time tuple formation rescues held-out `Q`; if the wall is the downstream combination itself, tuple and atomic-store arms both fail. Pair-key derangement and constituent-value permutation must collapse it.

This relocates binding to M’s missing write path without precomputing the gold.

4. Conditional: latent-variable graph join

Store degree-matched edges for `R(a,x)` and `S(x,b)`; the shared `x` is absent from the prompt. Ask whether a witness exists.

Prediction: a permutation-equivariant M join succeeds on held-out graphs, while edge shuffle preserving degree, marginal `R`/`S` counts and template bytes collapses to chance.

I call this conditional because it is a genuinely different target, but it should open only after fixed-pair arity-2 works. Before that, it adds search and set-intersection failure modes to an unresolved two-read problem.

I would not propose another VSA/TPR/bilinear head, denser corpus, deeper trunk, scale rung, untrained recurrence, or selection/veto mechanism; those would be kill-list reruns.

## Is G1’s goal wrong?

There is a coherent reading under which it is.

The wall may be real, while “make a next-byte trunk internalize arbitrary mutable facts and execute database-like joins from its weights” is the wrong systems objective. Runtime facts are naturally memory state, not model parameters. Under that reading:

```text
mutable facts → M
content addresses → trained lookup
relation/execution → D
answer + provenance → mouth
```

H_9775 is then not a workaround; it is the first correctly factored architecture. G1 should measure an arity frontier, adversarial address robustness, causal value dependence and provenance—not demand that all of these emerge inside the trunk.

The limitation is equally important: an engineered M→D XOR lane would demonstrate faithful online composition, not general creativity, consciousness, or spontaneous relational reasoning. If G1’s intended claim is specifically “anima can combine arbitrary runtime facts reliably,” the store experiment is correct. If the intended claim is “recombination must emerge endogenously from the monolithic language substrate,” then the campaign has conflated an architectural preference with the faculty being measured.
